title: Come, Wisdom, Power, and Grace Divine
description: Come, Wisdom, Power, and Grace Divine in Tonic Solfa to HOLY MATRIMONY, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 527.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Particular Metre (8.8.6.8.8.6), and this page sets them to HOLY MATRIMONY; any other Common Particular Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Come, wis-dom, power, and grace di-vine, Come, Je-sus, in thy name to join A hap-py cho-sen band; Who fain would prove thine ut-most will, And all thy right-eous laws ful-fil, In love's be-nign com-mand.

lines: Come, wisdom, power, and grace divine,
Come, Jesus, in thy name to join
Who fain would prove thine utmost will,
And all thy righteous laws fulfil,
If pure essential love thou art,
Bid all our simple souls be one,
Still may we to our centre tend,
To spread thy praise our common end,
To share a moment's pain, and seize
The pity of the bleeding Lamb,
The virtues of thy wondrous name,
The heart that was in thee.
To found the fellowship of saints,
So shall we all thy love receive,

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to HOLY MATRIMONY by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
